item.title: Learning to Prefer: The Human Whisper in Autonomous Microscopy
item.description: A human expert’s pairwise image comparisons teach an autonomous microscope which ferroelectric domain walls are scientifically most promising.

item.title: The Medical Map That Learned to Remember Time
item.description: A temporal biomedical knowledge graph encodes when symptoms emerge along disease trajectories, enabling machines and clinicians to grasp the story of illness over time.

item.title: Ghost Imaging Learns to See in the Mid-Infrared
item.description: Mid-infrared temporal ghost imaging is achieved at room temperature by using two-photon absorption in a silicon photodiode as an optoelectronic mixer.

item.title: The Algebra That Self-Tests Quantum Embezzlement
item.description: Exact entanglement embezzlement is a self-test for a pair of Cuntz algebras and a quasi-free state, revealing a unique type III factor.

item.title: Watching Entanglement Forget: The Crosscap Quench
item.description: In a crosscap quench, a topologically entangled system forgets its antipodal pairing as entanglement entropy grows linearly, transforming its quantum memory.

item.title: Nesting Carbon: Netsene and the Hidden Nodal-Surface Semimetal
item.description: Extending the Dirac physics of two-dimensional (2D) graphene into three dimensions (3D) carbon allotropes with higher-dimensional band degeneracies remains a central challenge in topological materials science. Here, we propose a general symmetry-engineering principl...

item.title: Light Hides a One‑Way Surface Channel
item.description: A single topological twist in the vacuum traps light as a one-way surface wave, even though the material on both sides is empty space.

item.title: Transporting Fluctuations: A New Theorem Preserves Hyperuniformity
item.description: A new theorem proves that hyperuniform point sets retain their suppressed fluctuations under gentle transport, enabling efficient generation of isotropic patterns with extreme order.

item.title: The Impossibility That Turns Explanations into a Coin Toss
item.description: A mathematical coin toss emerges when correlated features in machine learning models defy stable explanation, as proven by a new impossibility theorem.

item.title: How Drones Learn to Race, Overtake, and Avoid Crashing
item.description: Drones trained with league-based multi-agent reinforcement learning learn to overtake and avoid crashes, outperforming human champions in high-speed races.

item.title: When a Designed Key Ignores the Lock: Antigen Blindness in Antibody AI
item.description: AI antibody models often produce generic keys that ignore their target antigen, a failure called antigen blindness.

item.title: A Fireball’s Portrait: How Magnetars Paint with Curved Spacetime
item.description: A computational model decodes how magnetar fireballs imprint curved spacetime and quantum vacuum birefringence onto polarized X-ray bursts, linking stellar mass to light geometry.

item.title: EUV Holography Learns to Print Curved Patterns at 40 nm
item.description: A lensless EUV holography system prints arbitrary curvilinear patterns at 40 nm resolution, surpassing the periodic limit of interference lithography.

item.title: Climbing the Spin Glass with the Hessian’s Whisper
item.description: A new algorithm, Potential Hessian Ascent, uses free probability to listen to the curvature of the spin-glass landscape and reach the Parisi ground state.

item.title: The Radio Glow That Shouldn’t Have Survived: MeerKAT’s Peek into the Early Universe
item.description: MeerKAT's L-band observations reveal luminous radio halos in merging galaxy clusters at redshift >1, challenging models of cosmic microwave background energy losses.

item.title: When an Electron’s Recoil Becomes a Quantum Computer
item.description: An electron's discrete recoil upon absorbing photons creates a programmable quantum ladder, enabling universal quantum computation and black hole simulation.

item.title: Taming Rydberg Decay: A Smarter Way to Protect Quantum Information
item.description: Rydberg decay errors in neutral atom qubits are located and corrected using the final measurement pattern in a topological cluster state.

item.title: When Copper and Oxygen Dance: Building a Quantum Simulator for High-Temperature Superconductivity
item.description: A bichromatic optical superlattice traps ultracold atoms to simulate the copper-oxygen interactions in cuprate high-temperature superconductors.

item.title: The Quantum Adapter That Learned to Improve Language
item.description: A quantum circuit adapter improves language model performance by inserting two-qubit unitary blocks into frozen transformer layers.

item.title: A Shape That Protects: Can Topology Be Independent of Symmetry?
item.description: Higher-order topological phases (HOTPs) feature protected gapless modes on boundaries of higher codimension, such as the corners or hinges of a crystal. They are understood as being protected by lattice symmetries: If the latter are broken, it becomes possible to re...

item.title: How a 2D Code Learned Magic
item.description: A two-dimensional stabilizer code reaches beyond its dimensional ceiling, using cup products to weave a transversal T-gate directly into the fabric.

item.title: The Market That Eats Its Own Tail: Synthetic Data's Economic Trap
item.description: A self-consuming data serpent symbolizes the market failure where synthetic training data degrades model quality, creating an economic equilibrium of contamination.

item.title: When Symmetry Learns to Read the Data
item.description: A new starG tensor algebra extracts hidden symmetry from molecular data, decomposing properties into irreducible representation channels without prior physical knowledge.

item.title: The Chern Hierarchy: Graphene Learns to Count Its Layers
item.description: In rhombohedral graphene, the topological Chern number equals the number of layers, enabling electrical control of orbital magnetism without magnetic fields.

item.title: From Flat to Narrow: How a Lattice Remembers and Forgets
item.description: A Lieb lattice’s flat band traps a quantum emitter’s photon in a bound state, but symmetry breaking warps the band, enabling a switch from memory to forgetfulness.

item.title: Tuning Electrons Between Layers: Controlled Charge Transfer in Moiré Superlattices
item.description: A vertical electric field precisely controls the transfer of electrons between layers in a MoSe₂/WS₂ moiré superlattice.

item.title: Electrons Learn to Twist: How Zero‑Point Motion Builds a Quasicrystal
item.description: Zero‑point motion stabilizes a 30‑degree twisted bilayer quasicrystal of electrons, a new electronic phase in homogeneous quantum wells.

item.title: When Critics Are Right: Demanding Review Predicts Higher Impact
item.description: Papers that withstand the most demanding peer review, with strong, high-quality critiques, later earn significantly higher citations, challenging the view of review as mere gatekeeping.

item.title: When a Current Pulse Teaches a Magnet to Forget
item.description: A current pulse heats a 2D magnet above its Curie temperature, letting a weak magnetic field rewrite its magnetization without lasers.

item.title: The Wolf That Wasn’t? Quantum Spin Ice on a Superconducting Chip
item.description: Magnetic monopoles in artificial spin ice on a superconducting qubit array display super-diffusive motion, hinting at quantum coherence beyond classical diffusion.
